sentences.text: The only known species in the genus Venenosaurus is Venenosaurus dicrocei, a relatively small sauropod similar to the contemporary Cedarosaurus from Utah.
This small titanosauriform sauropod measured 12 meters in length and weighed 6 metric tons.
The genus name Venenosaurus derives from the Latin word for poison, referencing the Poison Strip Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation where it was found.
Unusual deep lateral depressions, or fossae, appeared on the outside walls of its tail vertebrae, with some divided into two chambers by an internal ridge.
The animal is uniquely identified by its flat-tailed vertebrae, known as amphiplatyan, with neural spines angled toward the front.
It remains uncertain whether fragmentary fossils from Dalton Wells Quarry belong to Venenosaurus or its close relative Cedarosaurus.
Venenosaurus possessed a more slender radius compared to other sauropods like Alamosaurus and Saltasaurus, and its metacarpals were long and slender in structure.
The pelvic structure of Venenosaurus most closely resembles that of Brachiosaurus.
Researchers suggest Venenosaurus may have possessed a vertebral condition intermediate between primitive and derived titanosaurs.
Venenosaurus belongs to the family Brachiosauridae and is classified within the class Saurischia.
Venenosaurus lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
